name: workspace-mixed
purpose: An okg-workspace-like deployment: 30 sources in every state, three enrichers including one withheld, four views including one that failed, several published versions and one attempt still running.
edge_cases: Every producer state in one table: updated, failed, running, never run, excluded (S18, S21).
An enricher withheld with a stated reason, and a view whose build failed with a four-line error (S19).
One source contributed zero records in the selected version, shown as 0 rather than blank (S7).
A 78-character source name that must truncate without hiding its distinguishing tail.
A cadence on half the sources, so 'next due' is populated for some rows and empty for others (S9).
A policy-hidden field on two records; Fields says hidden and names the policy, Raw shows it masked (S15).
One record whose retained payload is present and one whose payload policy refuses (S14); the same policy refuses that record's original file.
Real artifacts on disk: a PDF with three document_chunk records, a Markdown document, a Rust file, an HTML page and a PNG, each rendered on the Content tab.
A session whose retained payload is 350 KB, past the raw read's 256 KB inline limit, so Raw shows the first 200 lines and offers the file.
Several published versions, so the version picker has something to switch between (S16).
An attempt still running now (S3's running case).

results.label: Abstract (chunk 0)
results.excerpt: Operational knowledge graphs record what an engineering organisation did, decided and observed, so that the next question can be answered from evidence rather than from memory. We describe a substrate that ingests sources into a versioned graph, publishes each version only after its invariants hold, and serves reads pinned to one published version.

results.label: 1 Introduction (chunk 1)
results.excerpt: A deployment is a set of producers: sources that read external systems, enrichers that add relationships, and views that derive tables. An update attempt runs every producer, checks the result and publishes a version or blocks with a stated cause. Readers always see one published version at a time and can name which one they read.

results.label: 2 Retained payloads and artifacts (chunk 2)
results.excerpt: A source may retain the canonical record it ingested as JSON, chunked at one mebibyte with a byte count and a SHA-256. The original artifact, when the source keeps a corpus root, stays on disk under the path the record names. Both are served under the policy that masks the record's attributes, so an original file never bypasses the masking applied to its fields.

# Operator handbook

How to run the deployment day to day. Read **Home** first; it says whether the
last update published and what needs attention.

## Daily check

1. Open Home and read the status line.
2. If an attempt is blocked, open it in Updates and read the recorded error.
3. Open Sources for the producer it stopped on.

## Producers

| Producer | Kind | Cadence |
|---|---|---|
| `source-07-git` | source | every 6 h |
| `semantic-linker` | enricher | after every update |
| `daily-brief` | view | daily |

## Publishing by hand

```bash
okg update run --deployment workspace-mixed
okg generation describe <id> --invariants
```

- A version publishes only when every invariant holds.
- Reads keep serving the previous version until then.

See the [status page](https://docs.example.invalid/status) for the live view.

Operational knowledge graphs record what an engineering organisation did, decided and observed, so that the next question can be answered from evidence rather than from memory. We describe a substrate that ingests sources into a versioned graph, publishes each version only after its invariants hold, and serves reads pinned to one published version.

1 Introduction
A deployment is a set of producers: sources that read external systems, enrichers that add relationships, and views that derive tables. An update attempt runs every producer, checks the result and publishes a version or blocks with a stated cause. Readers always see one published version at a time and can name which one they read.

2 Retained payloads and artifacts
A source may retain the canonical record it ingested as JSON, chunked at one mebibyte with a byte count and a SHA-256. The original artifact, when the source keeps a corpus root, stays on disk under the path the record names. Both are served under the policy that masks the record's attributes, so an original file never bypasses the masking applied to its fields.

# Operator handbook

How to run the deployment day to day. Read **Home** first; it says whether the
last update published and what needs attention.

## Daily check

1. Open Home and read the status line.
2. If an attempt is blocked, open it in Updates and read the recorded error.
3. Open Sources for the producer it stopped on.

## Producers

| Producer | Kind | Cadence |
|---|---|---|
| `source-07-git` | source | every 6 h |
| `semantic-linker` | enricher | after every update |
| `daily-brief` | view | daily |

## Publishing by hand

```bash
okg update run --deployment workspace-mixed
okg generation describe <id> --invariants
```

- A version publishes only when every invariant holds.
- Reads keep serving the previous version until then.

See the [status page](https://docs.example.invalid/status) for the live view.
